chunks: My father and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan both narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Īsā, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

Fāṭimah (peace be upon her) came to the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family) and saw that his eyes were filled with tears. She asked him, 'What is the matter with you?' He replied, 'Jabraʾīl (peace be upon him) informed me that my nation will kill Ḥusayn.' She became extremely grieved and restless. So he informed her of those from her children who would hold authority. This pleased her and relieved her.

key_terms.حُسَيْنٌ: Husayn ibn Ali, the grandson of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What news did the Prophet receive from Jabraʾīl regarding Ḥusayn that caused Fāṭimah distress?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the prophetic foreknowledge of the Ahl al-Bayt's suffering, specifically linking the martyrdom of Ḥusayn (a.s.) to the broader concept of *Ummah* (community) rather than just his immediate family. The comfort provided to Fāṭimah (a.s.) by enumerating the Imams from her lineage underscores the Shia doctrine of *Nass* (designation), illustrating how divine authority serves as the consolation for earthly loss. This event is often cited by scholars to demonstrate the emotional depth of the Prophet and the continuity of leadership through the Twelve Imams.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 5. My father and Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan both narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan Al-Saffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Ibn Faďďāl, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:

(Once) Fāťimah (s.a.) came to the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) and saw that his eyes were filled with tears. She asked him, “What is upsetting you?” He replied, “Jabra`īl informed me that my nation will kill Ḥusain.” (When Fāťimah (s.a.) heard this), she became extremely grieved and restless. So the Prophet (s.a.a.w.) informed her of (the Imams from) her children who would reign. This (news) pleased her and relieved her.
